neet_che_u12_t02_1.working: K4[Fe(CN)6] has an anionic complex. K is +1, so Fe is +2. An anionic complex takes the Latin stem with -ate, giving ferrate(II): potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II).

neet_che_u12_t02_2.working: Ligands go in alphabetical order, ammine before chlorido. Co = +3 (5×0 − 1 + Co = +2). The complex is a cation, so there is no -ate ending: pentaamminechloridocobalt(III) chloride.

neet_che_u12_t02_3.working: Three oxalate ligands give 3×(−2) = −6. With Fe(III) the complex charge is −3, so three K+ are needed: K3[Fe(C2O4)3].

neet_che_u12_t02_4.working: The name is tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride. Ammine comes before aqua alphabetically (m before q), and the prefix tetra is ignored when ordering. A is true, R is true, and R explains A.

neet_che_u12_t02_5.working: Statement I: Ni(CO)4 is neutral, Ni is 0, so it is tetracarbonylnickel(0) with no -ate ending; correct. Statement II: [Co(en)3]3+ is a cation with Co(III), named tris(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) sulphate; correct.
